newsitem.title: USA: Pages sees revs rising for fall season.
newsitem.headline: Pages sees revs rising for fall season.

text.p: Pages Inc, a publisher of leisure books and textbooks, said Tuesday it expects its revenues to increase "substantially" for the fall season as it benefits from its Corporate and Good Book fairs.
S. Robert Davis, chairman, made the forecast as the company reported revenues for the first quarter dipping to $7.1 million from $9.5 million in the comparable quarter last year.
The company said it posted a net loss of $239,626 or $0.04 for the quarter, compared with a net income of $3.57 million or $0.62 in the similar period in 1996.
Davis said Pages has implemented several initiatives intended to significantly improve the company's long-term performance.
"We are very encouraged by initial results from these actions, including the reduction in operating loss on lower revenues for the most recent quarter, he said.
The company noted that income for the first quarter of 1997 included a non-cash reduction of expense of $431,287 to record the current value of stock appreciation rights issued in 1996.
At the same time, income for the first quarter of 1996 includes recognition of a $3.3 million gain from the sale of the company's United Kingdom distribution channel.

Also included in the income for the 1996 quarter was a $994,664 increase in income from cumulative effect of a change in accounting principle in connection with the discontinued operations of CA Short Co, it said.
